title: edikt phasea dispatch journal line
description: One line of the append-only .edikt/state/phasea-dispatch.jsonl journal (AC-018-2) — this schema describes a single journaled event object, not the file as a whole. A line is appended for every plan emission, every verify call, every consume, and every refusal at either plan or verify time (SP-006 §7's state machine), so the journal is the auditable spend ledger at both ends of the dispatch budget. Mirrors the append-only-JSONL pattern already established by tools/edikt/internal/hookmatch/journal.go's hook journal, for the same reason: an appended line survives a concurrent write under O_APPEND without a lock, and a rewritten state file can lose the record it just wrote.

schema_version.description: Contract version for this journal line's on-disk shape. Integer, matching the plan and receipt schemas' convention. Added per the SPEC-013 pre-flight correction: the journal was the only append-only format of the three phasea artifacts lacking a schema_version, leaving a future shape change with no way to distinguish an old line from a new one when the two are interleaved in the same append-only file.

event.description: "plan" — `phasea plan` emitted a plan file. "verify" — `phasea verify` ran and produced a receipt (whether or not it was all-ok). "consume" — a verify call resulted in consumed:true (the terminal success transition). "refuse" — dispatch was refused before doing the work it was asked to do: at plan time when the stale count exceeds phasea.ceiling or phasea.force_ceiling (AC-018-1), or at verify time when the plan_id is unknown or already consumed (AC-013-4). Every "refuse" event carries a `cause` field naming which of these it was.

plan_id.description: The plan this event concerns. Present even for a plan-time "refuse" event: plan_id is derived from corpus_hash + config_hash alone (see phasea-dispatch-plan.v2.schema.json), so it is computable whether or not a plan file was actually written — recording it ties the refusal to the specific corpus/config state that would have produced that plan.

items.description: Item count relevant to this event: the plan's item count for "plan"/"verify"/"consume" events, or the stale-sidecar count that was refused (which may exceed the applied ceiling) for a plan-time "refuse" event. 0 is valid only for a verify-time "refuse" (unknown or already-consumed plan_id — no items were evaluated).

failing.description: item_ids not at status "ok" as of this event. Empty for "plan" (nothing has been verified yet) and for "consume" (all-ok by definition). Populated for a "verify" event that found incomplete items, and for a plan-time "refuse" this is empty (the refusal happened before any item could be evaluated).

cause.description: Populated only on a "refuse" event (see the if/then below), naming which of the four refusal reasons applied. Plan-time causes: "ceiling-exceeded" — the stale count exceeded phasea.ceiling on the default (non-forced) path. "force-ceiling-exceeded" — the stale count exceeded phasea.force_ceiling on a `--force` run. Verify-time causes: "unknown-plan-id" — the plan_id named on the `phasea verify --plan <id>` invocation does not match any emitted plan. "already-consumed" — the named plan_id's receipt already has consumed:true (AC-013-4's re-verify rejection). Added per the SPEC-013 pre-flight correction: without this field, every refuse event collapsed into one undifferentiated journal line, and a plan-time budget refusal was indistinguishable from a verify-time replay-protection refusal by grepping the journal alone. Widened 2026-08-20: SPEC-013 SR-006 requires EVERY refusal to journal, and the original four causes covered only ceiling refusals — leaving prompt_version UNKNOWN, corpus load failure, item validation failure, pin-capture failure and invalid config as refusals that left no audit trace. FR-018 asks for auditable spend at both ends; a refusal nobody can see is not auditable. Additive enum members are non-breaking within a major version (templates/schemas/README.md). Widened again 2026-10-04 (#11; SPEC-013 revision of that date), additively: "sidecar-absent-on-request" — a requested extraction (`--artifact`) found no sidecar and no `--bootstrap` declaration (D414), which plan.go journaled from 0.9.0 dev builds without the value ever reaching this enum; "plan-id-terminal" — the corpus path derived the id of a plan that is already consumed or FAILED (a requested extraction derives a successor instead); "unclosed-plan" — the latest plan covering an item was never closed (dispatched and not restored, mid-retry, or FAILED) and the item's sidecar has moved since that plan pinned it.

ts.description: ISO8601 UTC timestamp of this journal event. Journal entries are audit history, not compiled governance output, so ADR-020's byte-determinism rule does not bind this field — same exemption as the receipt's verified_at.
